answer: PC1 (31.8% of variance) in the PCA on the 12 forms of capital in 100-year slices is a general "capital level" axis. The Middle Neolithic (3400–3000 BCE) is characterized by a steep decline on PC1: from a relatively high −0.62 in 3400–3300 BCE (boosted by a house-size peak, Z = +2.05, and positive copper/gold) down to the phase minimum −1.85 in 3200–3100 BCE, with a partial rebound to −1.53 in 3100–3000 BCE (net ≈ −0.9 SD): a phase that starts with elevated capital and loses it within two centuries, the trough coinciding with an axes/celts peak. The Younger Neolithic (2900–2300 BCE) is characterized by persistently low, essentially flat PC1 scores (−1.6 to −1.3; net ≈ +0.2 SD), with no sustained trend except a short-lived spike to −0.75 in 2700–2600 BCE driven by a monument-count outlier (ZMonument = +3.95). Against the full 4300–500 BCE series (PC1 range −2.0 to +4.5), both phases sit at negative PC1 levels far below the Late Neolithic (mean +0.54) and Bronze Age (OBA +2.95, YBA +1.87), so both Neolithic phases are low-capital intervals: the MN as a declining phase (from a house-size-driven high to a two-century low), the YN as a low, stable phase punctuated by a single monument-count event.

payload.workflow: Loaded data/capital.csv (39 rows, BCE 4300..500 at 100-year steps; comma decimals parsed; 12 pre-standardized Z-columns, 0 missing). Verified bin anchoring against data/time_series_data.csv (grid value at CE=-X applies to bin X-(X-100) BCE). Ran one SVD-PCA across all 39 slices x 12 variables on the pre-standardized columns (sign fixed so largest |loading| positive); read off PC1 scores for MN bins 3400-3300..3100-3000 and YN bins 2900-2800..2400-2300. Robustness: (a) within-window re-standardized PCAs per window (constant-in-window variables dropped), (b) per-capital-type PCAs using the approved mapping (Symbolic=ZAxtSchwert,ZDolch,Zhausgr; Social=ZCU_AU,Zamber,ZMonument; Cultural=ZKeform,Zkeverz; Economic=ZHort,ZSichel,ZBeil,ZMW). Artifacts: executed script pca_analysis.py, per-bin score table pca_scores_table.csv, loading table pca1_loadings.csv.
